text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a spike of target registration failures against our NLB-backed private endpoints in ap-northeast-1 after the autoscaler kicked new GPU nodes. Errors like "Target not registered" and 502s for a few minutes.
lee: Is this the VPCE-backed NLB for inference-prod?
maria: yes, customer-prod account, VPCE id vpce-0a1b2c3d, target group arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ap-northeast-1:123456789012:targetgroup/prod-nodes/abcd1234. We saw ~300 nodes join over ~90s which looks like we hit a registration throttle.
jordan: That explains the brief 503s. AWS has soft limits on target registration throughput and targets per NLB/targetgroup. We should request a quota bump and add a short-term mitigation.
sam: Can we stagger node attaches on scale-up? Add jitter to the kube-controller or the autoscaler hooks?
maria: good idea — I can patch the scaleup hook to sleep random(0,8s) before registering. Quick mitigation while we file with AWS.
lee: What quota do we request? Is it targets-per-nlb or target-registration-rate? Need the exact quota code for the support ticket.
jordan: From previous chats: ask for increased "Targets per Network Load Balancer" and also a higher "target registration rate" if they offer it. Include explanation: autoscale event produced concentrated attach bursts causing transient failures, we serve low-latency requests so rolling failures matter.
cloud-ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE — brief 503 spike recorded 1842012300-1842012400, affected ~2% of requests to /generate. Root cause: NLB target registration throttling during node scale-up.
maria: I drafted the support case body — can one of you sanity-check before I submit?

maria: ---support case draft---
We are Redwood Inference; account 123456789012. Region ap-northeast-1. Our NLB (arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ap-northeast-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/net/inference-prod/abcd1234) backs a target group used by EC2/GKE nodes in a private VPC via VPC Endpoints. During large autoscaling events (hundreds of nodes within ~2 minutes) we observe target registration failures and transient 5xx responses due to registration throttling. Please increase our quota for Targets per NLB and target registration rate for ap-northeast-1 to support bursty autoscale patterns. Recommended temporary increase to 5000 targets and raise registration throughput to accommodate ~1000 attaches/minute. We also request guidance on account-level limits for VPCE target attachments.
---end---

sam: suggestion: add our mitigation plan (stagger attach, pre-warm target groups by provisioning warm nodes) and ask if there are recommended best practices for VPCE+NLB high-churn fleets. Makes them more likely to approve.
jordan: Also include timeframe sensitive ask: need soft increase for next 48–72 hours while we roll a safer scale strategy.
lee: I'll add the support template and submit. After submit, open an internal ticket to track AWS case id + rollout plan.
maria: submitted — case id 1234-5678-9012. AWS engineer asked for our CloudWatch metrics and a HAR of registration failures. Pasted timeline and sample logs.
lee: thanks. I created a short runbook: (1) patch autoscaler hook to add jitter, (2) pre-create 50 warm nodes during business hours for large promos, (3) monitor target registration errors via CloudWatch alarm -> pager.
cloud-ops-bot: RUNBOOK CREATED — /runbooks/nlb-registration-backoff.md (internal link) :white_check_mark:
jordan: After quota bump is confirmed we'll remove warm nodes and revert. For long term, product should consider smoother ramping for big experiments.
devops-bot: Deploy queued: autoscaler-hook-jitter v2 will roll to staging in 10m.
maria: keeping this thread for traceability. Will post AWS case updates here. :thumbsup:
lee: AWS updated the case requesting sample timestamps and the number of simultaneous attaches — I uploaded metrics and a few example logs.
maria: AWS approved a temporary increase for 72 hours, reviewer asked for architecture notes for permanent raise. Marking as partial win.
jordan: Great — after we finish the controlled scale tests, let's request a permanent quota bump with the production metrics attached.
lee: closing loop — no more 5xx spikes after jitter rollout and the temp bump, monitoring green for 24h.
maria: thanks all. Will file a retrospective doc with numbers and next actions. :party_popper:
